title: From Discovery to Process Control: Positioning DIA Proteomics in Biomanufacturing Pipelines
projectDescription: This project benchmarks five DIA-based LC–MS platforms for their ability to quantify proteins in E. coli and Halomonas bluephagenesis under biomanufacturing‑relevant conditions. Using simple peptide ratio mixtures and an exemplar carbon source comparison, it shows how instruments across a range of costs can still deliver actionable coverage of core metabolic pathways. The work is aimed at positioning quantitative proteomics as a practical tool for chassis selection, process development, and troubleshooting in industrial biomanufacturing.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Bacterial pellets from E. coli and Halomonas bluephagenesis were thawed and lysed in SDS/TEAB S‑Trap buffer, with DNA digested using benzonase before clearing debris and performing buffer exchange to remove contaminants. Proteins were reduced, alkylated, and digested on S‑trap mini columns with trypsin, and peptide yield was quantified fluorometrically to normalise concentrations. Fixed‑ratio mixtures of E. coli and Halomonas digests (1:1, 1:2, 2:1) and single‑species samples were then prepared, aliquoted, lyophilised, and reconstituted in LC loading buffer; an additional high‑pH C18 fractionation was performed to generate spectral library material for the Vion.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files from timsTOF, Exploris, ZenoTOF and MRT were processed with DIA‑NN using a combined E. coli + H. bluephagenesis FASTA, 1% q‑value threshold, standard tryptic settings, carbamidomethyl C, Met oxidation, and match‑between‑runs enabled; MRT data were first denoised and centroided with OpenMS. DIA‑NN report files were converted to MSstats input format in R, then analysed with MSstats to obtain absolute protein abundance estimates and differential expression statistics for all DIA‑processed instruments. For the Vion, fractionated samples were searched via Waters PLGS to build a spectral library, false discovery rates were controlled with MAYU, and production runs were processed in Skyline to generate MSstats‑compatible quantification tables that were analysed alongside the DIA‑NN outputs.
